title: PACHA_Backdoor_Investigation_d12
description: Your organization has detected suspicious activity on several Linux servers. Initial analysis suggests the presence of the PACHA backdoor malware, known for its coinmining capabilities, persistence mechanisms, and lateral movement. Your task is to investigate, analyze, and respond to this cybersecurity incident.
outcomes: Identify and investigate unauthorized or suspicious services.
Determine persistence mechanisms used by the malware.
Analyze network traffic for command-and-control (C2) communication.
Collect forensic evidence and contain the threat.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: Your organization has detected suspicious activity on several Linux servers. Initial analysis suggests the presence of the PACHA backdoor malware, known for its coinmining capabilities, persistence mechanisms, and lateral movement. Your task is to investigate, analyze, and respond to this cybersecurity incident. You will encounter various types of flags, including service names, persistence mechanisms, and C2 ports.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content: Access the target host via SSH using the following credentials: Username: cyrano, Password: cyrano.
levels.local_content: Access the target host via SSH using the following credentials: Username: cyrano, Password: cyrano.

levels.title: Suspicious Service Discovery
levels.content: While monitoring the network, you noticed unusual outbound connections from the target host. Investigate the host to identify any unauthorized or suspicious services running on it. Learning objective: Identify and investigate unauthorized or suspicious services. The flag is the name of the suspicious service.
levels.solution: To identify the suspicious service, you can use commands like `netstat -tuln` or `ss -tuln` to list all running services and their associated processes. Look for any services that are not part of the standard system configuration. The flag is the name of the suspicious service: pacha-service.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Check running services and their associated processes using `netstat -tuln` or `ss -tuln`.

hints.title: Directional Hint
hints.content: Look for any services that are not part of the standard system configuration.

hints.title: Near-Spoiler Hint
hints.content: The suspicious service name is pacha-service.

levels.title: Persistence Discovery
levels.content: Now that you have identified the suspicious service, determine how it is automatically started after a system reboot. This will help you understand the persistence mechanism used by the malware. Learning objective: Determine persistence mechanisms used by the malware. The flag is the name of the persistence mechanism.
levels.solution: To determine the persistence mechanism, investigate systemd services, cron jobs, or other scheduled tasks. Use commands like `systemctl list-units --type=service` to list all systemd services or `crontab -l` to list cron jobs. The flag is the name of the persistence mechanism: pacha-persistence.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Investigate systemd services, cron jobs, or other scheduled tasks using `systemctl list-units --type=service` or `crontab -l`.

hints.title: Directional Hint
hints.content: Look for any unusual or unauthorized services or tasks.

hints.title: Near-Spoiler Hint
hints.content: The persistence mechanism name is pacha-persistence.

levels.title: C2 Communication Discovery (Port)
levels.content: Analyze the network traffic to determine which port is used for the suspicious communication between the target host and the potential command-and-control server. Learning objective: Analyze network traffic for command-and-control (C2) communication. The flag is the C2 port number.
levels.solution: To analyze the network traffic, use network monitoring tools like `tcpdump` or `Wireshark` to inspect outgoing connections. Look for any connections to suspicious IP addresses or ports. The flag is the C2 port number: 4444.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Use network monitoring tools to inspect outgoing connections using `tcpdump -i any -n` or `Wireshark`.

hints.title: Directional Hint
hints.content: Look for connections to suspicious IP addresses or ports.
